topic: Research: Deploy Llama 4 with vLLM and Ollama: Scout vs Maverick Setup Guide

key_points: Ollama exposes dedicated commands for Scout and Maverick (`ollama run llama4:scout`, `ollama run llama4:maverick`) and describes multimodal inputs for Llama 4.
Official benchmark lines show Llama 4 Maverick outperforming Scout on MMLU Pro and Image reasoning metrics while Scout remains lighter.
vLLM announced support for Llama 4 (Scout and Maverick) and recommends v0.8.3+ for usage.
It provides serving examples by model and GPU topology, including context-length behavior (for example Scout up to 1M context on 8xH100, higher on H200) and accuracy parity checks with Meta evals.
Framing is still the strongest practical signal: Ollama for local low-concurrency setups and rapid prototyping, vLLM for production concurrency.
Highlights that Apple Silicon workflows often force Ollama because vLLM lacks Metal support.
Treats Ollama as llama.cpp with a wrapper and vLLM as a scaled production server with PagedAttention.
Claims vLLM handles significantly higher concurrent load than Ollama and is up to ~4x better for higher throughput scenarios.
Provides explicit feature and architecture comparison showing vLLM continuous batching and multi-GPU support versus Ollama sequential behavior.
Benchmarks report vLLM as far more concurrent at 32 users (420 tok/s vs 46 tok/s on RTX 3090 for sample model setup).

stats.fact: TechCrunch/Meta coverage describes Llama 4 Scout as a 17B active-parameter model with 16 experts (109B total) and Maverick as 17B active with 128 experts (400B total).
Ollama model page reports 400B total/17B active for Maverick and 109B total/17B active for Scout and shows benchmark scores on MMMU Pro, MathVista, LiveCodeBench, MMLU Pro, etc.

vLLM official post says vLLM added Llama 4 support (v0.8.3+) with long-context guidance: Scout up to 1M (with 8xH100, 1.0M) and Maverick up to ~430K for similar setup; up to 3.6M and 1M respectively on 8xH200.
On an RTX 3090 comparison, gigagpu reports vLLM and Ollama throughput differences from 1.2x at 1 concurrent user to 9.1x at 32 users, indicating clear concurrency scaling advantage.

Ollama’s model management page indicates native multimodality support with `ollama run llama4:maverick` and `ollama run llama4:scout`, with multilingual support and use-case intent for chat/vision/analysis.

angles: Build a strict decision matrix first: choose between Scout and Maverick by active parameters, expert count, context, latency budget, and GPU footprint.
Position vLLM as a production-serving path (continuous batching, tensor parallel) and Ollama as fast local dev path for one-off inference or small teams.
Exploit multimodality by testing image-heavy prompts, since both stacks differ in image routing behavior and max images per request handling.
Quantization strategy is now the highest-risk decision: FP8/NVFP4 with vLLM versus GGUF workflows in Ollama can swing memory and throughput for Scout/Maverick.
Long-context promises need hardware realism; compare claimed 10M token context with practical tested limits and memory behavior per stack.
